comparator.name: BSc Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme page presents a complete 180-EC curriculum: 60 EC in Year 1, 60 EC in Year 2 and 60 EC in Year 3. It names Econometrics, Operations Research, Actuarial Science and Mathematical Economics as profiles but presents one shared curriculum table rather than separate formal 180-EC routes, so no profile is instantiated as the comparator route. The 30-EC minor or study-abroad semester and the 5-EC programme elective remain explicit open-choice components.
components: Genuine approved minor or study-abroad space.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics and econometrics with mathematics, probability, programming, algorithms, optimisation and decision-making under uncertainty.
alternatives.concept: The closest UCR response combines mathematical and statistical foundations with econometrics, economics, programming, algorithms and optimisation. It reproduces the programme’s broad quantitative core while acknowledging that UCR does not offer Groningen’s sustained specialist econometrics and insurance sequences.
progression: Programming, economics and corporate-finance foundations begin in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods precede linear algebra, probability, econometrics and advanced quantitative work. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms, and the main mathematical and programming foundations precede optimisation and reinforcement learning. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Operations research, algorithms & decision systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres on programming, databases, algorithms, mathematical systems, optimisation, machine learning and computational decisions under uncertainty.
alternatives.concept: This route develops the official Operations Research direction through programming, databases, algorithms, mathematical modelling, optimisation, machine learning and sequential decision systems, with economics and organisational applications.
progression: Programming, data science, economics and business foundations precede software development, database work, algorithms, machine learning and advanced mathematical systems. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms; mathematical and programming foundations precede optimisation and reinforcement learning. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest curriculum, this route replaces macroeconomics, public economics, behavioural economics, ethics and part of the general econometric sequence with databases, software development, linear systems, neural networks and organisational decision work. These changes make computational operations research and algorithmic decision systems the organising centre.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, climate & public policy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics, econometrics and quantitative methods with climate change, circular economy, renewable systems, sustainability research and public policy.
alternatives.concept: This route uses econometrics and quantitative decision methods to examine climate, welfare and public-policy problems. Economics and statistics are combined with climate science, life-cycle analysis, renewable-system design and applied sustainability research.
progression: Programming, economics and sustainability foundations begin in Year 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods precede linear algebra, probability, econometrics and advanced modelling; Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes Renewable System Design. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest curriculum, this route replaces finance, discrete mathematics, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning and international macroeconomics with sustainability gateways, climate change, life-cycle analysis, renewable-system design and applied regional sustainability research. It also differs from the operations-research route through its environmental-science and public-policy application core.

blocks: Mathematical Methods provides calculus and related quantitative foundations, though it is broader than this dedicated calculus course.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistical modelling and research-design foundations in a broader applied setting.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations for quantitative modelling.
Probability & Statistics provides probability distributions, estimation and inference, though Groningen continues this material across several dedicated courses.
Statistics & Experimental Methods covers regression and multivariate modelling in a behavioural-science context.
Econometrics directly develops regression-based estimation, testing, prediction and causal analysis.
Advanced Calculus develops multivariable calculus and differential-equation methods.
Linear Systems develops advanced matrix and linear-systems reasoning relevant to this component.
Both provide introductory programming for quantitative problem solving; UCR uses Python.
Both introduce data preparation, analysis and visualisation; Groningen embeds these skills in its dedicated EOR sequence.
Computational & Numerical Methods directly develops numerical algorithms for mathematical problems.
Advanced Algorithms develops computational solution methods for discrete optimisation problems.
Optimization Methods in AI includes continuous optimisation among broader search and constraint methods.
Decision-making in AI treats planning and decisions under uncertainty, but does not reproduce the full stochastic-operations-research sequence.
Introduction to Economics provides the relevant microeconomic foundations, alongside macroeconomics.
Accounting & Corporate Finance provides financial-information and corporate-finance foundations.
International Macroeconomics directly develops macroeconomic analysis using theory and data.
Microeconomics & Behavior includes strategic behaviour and game-theoretic economic reasoning.
UCR has finance and quantitative decision courses, but no scheduled actuarial or insurance course equivalent.
UCR offers one dedicated econometrics course but not Groningen’s further dynamic-econometrics sequence.
UCR has finance and quantitative decision courses, but no scheduled actuarial or insurance course equivalent.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a genuine minor or study-abroad semester; the UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
Groningen requires a 10-EC thesis. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

candidates.label: Mathematical Economics, climate and public policy

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers the shared mathematical, statistical, econometric and economic core. The official Operations Research profile supports a distinct computational optimisation route, while the Mathematical Economics profile and programme-supported climate, welfare and public-policy problems support a distinct quantitative sustainability-and-policy route. The Actuarial Science direction was assessed separately but is not feasible because UCR lacks actuarial mathematics and insurance-risk courses. Three defensible alternatives are included, which is the maximum.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability and quantitative modelling
Operations research, optimisation and decisions under uncertainty
Economics, markets, finance and societal applications
Research practice, academic skills and responsible quantitative decisions
adjacent: Mathematical economics, climate, welfare and public policy
questions: How can economic and social problems be translated into mathematical models?
How can optimisation and statistical evidence improve decisions under uncertainty?
How can quantitative models inform climate, welfare and public-policy choices?

notes.text: Groningen provides a sustained specialist sequence in mathematics, econometrics, operations research and insurance. UCR can combine strong related courses in these areas, but does not reproduce the same disciplinary depth or actuarial sequence.
